dedupe_keys.name: us food supply chain energy use and greenhouse gas emissions database 2016

description: This database estimates the energy consumption and greenhouse gas emissions of the US food system, from farm production through processing, packaging, distribution, retail, food service and households to waste. It was built by researchers at Oak Ridge National Laboratory, the Department of Energy's Industrial Efficiency and Decarbonization Office, Texas State University and the University of Tennessee, and is described in an open-access article in npj Science of Food (2025). Results are given at national and state level by supply chain stage, fuel type and food commodity for 2016: the food supply chain used about 4,660 trillion Btu of site energy and 7,130 trillion Btu of primary energy and emitted 970 million tonnes of greenhouse gases, with on-farm production the largest share (31 percent of primary energy and 70 percent of emissions). The data are free in a public GitHub repository, and the article is under a Creative Commons Attribution licence; the input sources are all public. Caveats: the single base year predates recent shocks, and many values are modelled from national statistics. Simulation uses: energy demand of food supply chains in energy and food system interdependency and disruption models. Related records: the EDGAR-FOOD emissions database (data-edgar-food) gives global food system emissions, and FAOSTAT agrifood emissions shares (data-faostat-agrifood-emissions-shares) give country totals. Licence (read on 2026-09-29): MIT (repository); article CC-BY-4.0.
